item.title: Global Chess League: Viswanathan Anand loses to Carlsen on time; calls it 'a pity'
item.description: Magnus Carlsen edged Viswanathan Anand in a dramatic time scramble on Day 3 of the Global Chess League, with Anand losing on time despite his team securing victory. Carlsen later drew Javokhir Sindarov after unleashing the surprise 3...f6. Despite calling his form underwhelming, the World No. 1 praised Bengaluru’s passionate chess crowd as the tournament delivered another action-packed day.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Same salary, fewer duties after maternity leave; Delhi HC awards Rs 10 lakh
item.description: The High Court has made it clear that the statutory safeguard also covers the work she performs, her position in the organisational hierarchy, supervisory powers and opportunities for appraisal and promotion.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: In 2006, Google VP emailed Steve Jobs seeking permission to hire former Apple exec
item.description: A 2006 email thread surfaced by Internal Tech Emails shows Google senior VP Alan Eustace asking Steve Jobs for permission before hiring former Apple executive Jean-Marie Hullot in Paris. Jobs asked what Hullot would build, warning Google would have a problem if it involved cell phone handsets. Weeks later he objected outright, and Google scrapped the Paris engineering centre entirely. Tim Sweeney called it blatantly illegal.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: CCTV captures accused fleeing moments after Manipuri musician beaten to death in Delhi
item.description: A musician hailing from Manipur was fatally attacked by dhaba staff in Delhi after raising concerns about disruptive noise levels. The confrontation spiraled out of control, resulting in a brutal assault in an alleyway. After suffering grave injuries, the musician passed away during medical care. The police have arrested eight workers connected to this alarming incident.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Real estate firm told to pay customer Rs 60K a month over white sandalwood deal
item.description: A consumer commission ordered a real estate firm to pay monthly lease amounts. The company failed to honor a lease agreement for a sandalwood plantation investment. The customer invested Rs 17.5 lakh in 2023 for agricultural land. The commission awarded Rs 60,000 monthly, plus compensation and litigation costs. The company must comply with the order within 45 days.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Republican mayor rejects 'Lake America' name; says locals take renaming personally
item.description: The Republican mayor of Oswego has firmly opposed President Trump's executive order to rename Lake Ontario, emphasizing the importance of the lake's original name in shaping the community's identity. This decision has sparked bipartisan and international discontent among numerous political leaders, especially with the recent downturn in Canadian tourism to the U.S. Locals will persist in using the lake's historical name, rooted in Indigenous heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 'Sar tan se juda' challenges India's sovereignty: HC rejects Taukir Raza's bail plea
item.description: The Allahabad High Court denied bail to Maulana Tauqeer Raza concerning the 2025 Bareilly violence. The court found his speech challenged law and India's sovereignty and integrity. Raza was jailed in October 2025 following September's violent rally. Police reported he called for a large assembly without official permission. The court noted his post-incident speech applauded the crowd's actions.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: In 1895, lightning ignited West Virginia gas well, sending flames 200 feet high
item.description: In a remarkable display, a West Virginia gas well suffered a fiery explosion triggered by a lightning strike. Discovered in 1895, this vast gas reservoir was tough to control with the limited technology of the era. For two hours, flames leaped 150 to 200 feet into the sky until the force of the escaping gas extinguished itself.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: iPhone 18 launch event on September 9: How, when and where to watch
item.description: Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' event on September 9, 2026, will unveil the iPhone 18 series. The company is also launching its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Ultra, with a large display. New Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models are expected alongside updated AirPods. The event marks the first major public appearance for Apple's new CEO, John Ternus.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Ujjain tried to move 170-year-old Hanuman idol; 4 attempts failed
item.description: Ujjain's road-widening endeavor meets a unique obstacle with a cherished Hanuman idol. Heavy machinery's attempts to shift the ancient statue from its temple location have been futile. In light of this, officials are seeking guidance from archaeologists for a careful relocation strategy. Until then, the idol stays protected by a temporary canopy while devoted locals assemble, perceiving the incident as deeply spiritual.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Why thousands of US affordable homes are sitting vacant while renters remain homeless
item.description: Thousands of affordable housing units sit vacant across US cities. Poorest renters face severe housing shortages and high rental costs. Many subsidized homes target higher incomes, leaving the lowest earners with few choices. Developers find building for the poorest renters economically challenging without significant subsidies. This disparity leaves many individuals like Mathew Davis searching for a place to live.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Studies can wait, classrooms at DU turn shelters for displaced students
item.description: In response to a recent building collapse, Delhi University colleges quickly repurposed their facilities to serve as temporary shelters for students affected by the tragedy. These institutions provided essential services, including beds, meals, and counselling to those in distress. The incident led to the evacuation and sealing of several nearby private hostels over safety concerns.
item.dc:creator: SUGANDHA JHA

item.title: Ticketless woman held in Bihar with 75 litres of liquor in first AC coach
item.description: A young woman was discovered with a large liquor consignment in a locked train compartment. Railway officials found her with approximately seventy-five liters of foreign liquor. She and her relative were arrested and subsequently sent to judicial custody. Police are investigating her family's alleged involvement in similar liquor-related cases. Her phone contacts are also being examined for potential links to the liquor movement.
item.dc:creator: FARYAL RUMI

item.title: ‘Learn from Ishan Kishan’: Ex-India cricketer’s message to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
item.description: Ishan Kishan scored a remarkable double century in the Duleep Trophy final. He guided East Zone to a substantial score against South Zone. Kumar Kushagra also contributed a century to the team's total. East Zone's batting effort surpassed seven hundred runs in the match. Kishan's innings was a highlight of the Duleep Trophy final.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: Vanessa Trump and Tiger Woods’ $50m TGR Foundation: How did she support him?
item.description: In early 2026, Vanessa Trump graced Tiger Woods' charity birthday event, marking a milestone for the TGR Foundation, which announced an impressive fifty million dollars raised for education. Shortly after, she subtly celebrated the TGR Learning Lab's anniversary, reinforcing her connection to Woods' commendable community outreach. Her attendance underscored the foundation's growing influence on young learners, showcasing the vital role they play in education.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Tom Brady’s message to Hannah after Michigan debut: What did he say?
item.description: Hannah Brady finally made her Michigan volleyball debut against Valparaiso, and she started with an ace on her first serve. Michigan won 3-1, and Tom Brady responded with a simple “So proud of you” on Instagram. After spending her freshman year without a match appearance, Hannah now has her first college moment to build on for the first time.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Prince Harry begins work on mystery project at London studio
item.description: Prince Harry visited a London studio for an undisclosed project. He spent a full day working and signed the celebrity wall. This visit occurred as King Charles clarified the couple's royal status. The letter confirmed they are no longer working royals. They will also not use their royal highness titles.

item.title: Take it or leave it: Across Delhi, they put lives on line to study
item.description: Cramped living quarters in Delhi’s educational hubs pose serious safety challenges for students. Many pay high rents for tiny rooms near colleges and coaching centers, but the conditions can be alarming. In neighborhoods such as Laxmi Nagar and Mukherjee Nagar, issues like inadequate ventilation and open wiring abound. Recent incidents highlight the perilous environments shaped by narrow avenues and insufficient safety measures, impacting thousands of aspiring learners.
item.dc:creator: ISHITA JAIRATH

item.title: Ishan Kishan signals red-ball intent with mammoth 270
item.description: Kishan smashed 270 off 334 balls (30x4, 7x6), taking East to a mammoth 708 all out, Kumar Kushagra chipping in with 101 as well. The double century, his second in first-class cricket, came after a gap of 10 years and has further strengthened his case for a return to India's red-ball setup.
item.dc:creator: DIPTAYAN HAZRA

item.title: Brent crude climbs beyond $97 as Hormuz disruptions choke global oil supplies
item.description: With the ongoing conflict in the Middle East escalating, oil prices are experiencing a significant uptick as global supplies come under threat. Iran has issued warnings of retaliation against US actions, heightening fears surrounding energy infrastructure. As tensions rise in the Strait of Hormuz, traders are incorporating a risk premium into oil costs.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Don’t hurt Sanatani traditions, CM Suvendu tells Puja organisers
item.description: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari announced changes for Durga Puja celebrations this year. Organizers must adhere to original traditions and avoid themes that hurt heritage. The state will not hold an immersion carnival but will feature roadshows and a Mahalaya program. A partial ban on alcohol sales will be enforced, with liquor vends closed on Ashtami.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Night entry, lifting clothes don't amount to rape bid: Jharkhand HC
item.description: The Jharkhand High Court's decision emphasized that entering a woman's home after dark does not equate to attempted rape. The distinction made between criminally outrageous conduct and attempted rape is significant, resulting in upholding a conviction for offending modesty. The judge decided to lessen the sentence to time already served, thereby clarifying the legal nuances surrounding sexual offenses against women.
item.dc:creator: CHANDRAJIT MUKHERJEE

item.title: ‘Pakistan has gone back 10 years’: Saeed Ajmal launches scathing PCB attack
item.description: Saeed Ajmal, the former spinner from Pakistan, has voiced serious concerns regarding the Pakistan Cricket Board's management, asserting that it has demoralized players and stunted their development. He also shifted blame towards Aaqib Javed and Mike Hesson for the team's ongoing struggles. Meanwhile, the PCB chairman has stood firm in his justification of recent adjustments following a Test loss, especially as Pakistan endures a troubling whitewash against England.

item.title: 'North pole and south pole': Nehra compares Shubman Gill and Hardik Pandya
item.description: Shubman Gill took over as Gujarat Titans captain after Hardik Pandya left the franchise. He led the team to the IPL final in 2026, after Pandya and Nehra had guided GT to the title in their first season in 2022 and another final in 2023. Nehra said Gill and Pandya are very different personalities and leaders, but both have the ability to keep learning.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: After CWG bronze, Seema Kaliramna sets sights on another step towards Olympics at Asian Games
item.description: Seema Kaliramna returned to competition 11 months after giving birth to her son Rudra, after dealing with severe arthritis that left her unable to walk 10 metres or pick up her child. With husband and coach Ravinder by her side, she rebuilt her fitness and confidence, moving from 57.19m in 2024 to a 59.73m personal best this year and a Commonwealth Games bronze. Now, the Asian Games offer another step towards the Olympics.
